drhp.business: Bharat Seats manufactures automotive seats and seating systems for four-wheelers, supplying original-equipment vehicle makers. Its core customer is Maruti Suzuki India Limited, whose safety team and vendor programme are closely integrated with the Company's plants and quality culture. During the year the Company began supplying four-wheeler seats to Maruti Suzuki from its new Kharkhauda facility in Sonipat, Haryana.

drhp.expansion: Bharat Seats set up a new manufacturing facility at Kharkhauda in Sonipat, Haryana, and from April 2025 commenced supply of seats for four-wheelers to Maruti Suzuki India Limited from this plant. Management attributes improved performance to better capacity utilisation driven by increased sales of Car Seats to Maruti Suzuki India Limited together with cost-saving measures. There was no change in the nature of business during FY2025-26, and no material changes or commitments affecting the financial position occurred after year-end.

litigation.note: No significant or material orders passed by regulators, courts or tribunals that would impact the Company's going-concern status or future operations.

drhp.one_liner: Bharat Seats Limited is an automotive seating-systems maker whose fortunes are anchored to its long-standing supply relationship with Maruti Suzuki India Limited.

risks.note: Revenue growth and improved capacity utilisation are explicitly attributed to higher car-seat sales to Maruti Suzuki; the business is heavily dependent on this single OEM relationship, so any slowdown, volume cut or loss of share would directly impair performance.
risks.risk: Customer concentration on Maruti Suzuki India Limited

risks.note: From April 2025 the Company began supplying four-wheeler seats to Maruti Suzuki from the newly set-up Kharkhauda (Sonipat, Haryana) plant; utilisation, cost and ramp of this facility are execution-dependent.

The Company enters into contracts/transactions with related parties (in the ordinary course, at arm's length, disclosed in Form AOC-2); heavy reliance on group/promoter-linked dealings creates governance and pricing-scrutiny risk.
Finance costs rose over the year and the Company relies on external credit; its ICRA short-term A1 and long-term A (Stable) ratings must be maintained to preserve funding access and cost.

Promoters (Rohit, Ritu, Rishabh, Pranav and Ayush Relan) gifted 1,02,88,358 (16.38%) equity shares to a family trust in Sep 2025, shifting control from individual promoters to a trust for succession purposes; concentrated promoter/trust control is a durable governance consideration.
risks.risk: Change in control to Promoter Family Trust
